title: GCD: Euclid's Algorithm
contract: Return the nonnegative greatest common divisor for nonnegative a and b, not both zero.
brute: if(a==0)return b;if(b==0)return a;for(long d=Math.min(a,b);d>=1;d--){emit("Try a common divisor","candidate",d);if(a%d==0&&b%d==0)return d;}return 1;
optimal: while(b!=0){long remainder=a%b;emit("Replace the pair with divisor and remainder","pair",new long[]{a,b},"remainder",remainder);a=b;b=remainder;}return a;
reasoning: Test candidates descending until one divides both numbers.
A number divides both a and b exactly when it divides b and a mod b, so the set of common divisors is unchanged.
Remainders strictly decrease until zero. Compute LCM as (a/gcd)*b with an overflow check rather than multiplying first.
